clusters.search: "homes for sale in <town or community>": the /homes/near/<slug>/ IDX place pages, including the 13 town-* strips
clusters.owner: For a town: the town guide /submarkets/<town>/, carrying the horizontal IDX strip. For a named community: one /homes/near/<community>/ page per community.
clusters.problem: The 13 town-* places are correctly kept out of search. functions/homes/[[path]].js line 1051 sets robots "noindex, follow" (plus the x-robots-tag header) when place.index === false. functions/sitemap-homes.xml.js filters PLACES[s].index !== false. idx-lib/places.js has "index": false on all 13 town-* slugs, and none of them appears in GSC. The other 63 place pages are indexed and in the sitemap, and several of them cannibalize. (1) Exact duplicates: /homes/near/tidewater/ and /homes/near/tidewater-plantation/ are both titled "Homes for sale in Tidewater Plantation" and both show in GSC (11 and 9 impressions, position 60 to 69). /homes/near/golf-and-yacht-club/ and /homes/near/myrtle-beach-golf-and-yacht-club/ run the identical query (subdivision "Golf and Yacht") under the identical title. (2) Same title, different filter: nohoa-cherry-grove and cherry-grove are both "Homes for sale in Cherry Grove". nohoa-garden-city-beach and second-home-garden-city-beach are both "Homes for sale in Garden City Beach". nohoa-ocean-drive and second-home-north-myrtle-beach center on the same point (33.82231,-78.67907). (3) Filtered slices with a whole-town title: nohoa-conway, nohoa-loris, nohoa-little-river, nohoa-socastee, nohoa-aynor, nohoa-surfside-beach, second-home-murrells-inlet, second-home-pawleys-island and second-home-north-myrtle-beach are titled "Homes for sale in Conway" (and so on). They show only no-HOA houses within 0.5 to 3 miles, or a 1.5-mile beach circle, and they compete with the town guides, whose JSON-LD targets "<town> homes for sale". (4) The site search sends readers to the wrong page. idx-lib/query.js resolves a bare town name to the first matching place in PLACES order, so "homes in Conway" 302s to /homes/near/nohoa-conway/ (no-HOA houses only), not to the town-conway strip. The same happens for Loris, Little River, Socastee, Aynor, North Myrtle Beach (second-home) and Murrells Inlet (second-home).
clusters.fix: In Blog-Brain batches/2026-10-b/data/idx-places.json, then regenerate idx-lib/places.js: (a) Set "index": false on all 16 nohoa-* and all 5 second-home-* places. These are strips for one guide each, which is the reason the town-* places are noindex. (b) Keep one Tidewater slug. Keep tidewater-plantation, whose name matches the search "tidewater plantation real estate". Confirm which subdivision words return the right MLS set, point the strip on /buyers/best-neighborhoods/ at it, and add a 301 from /homes/near/tidewater/. (c) Keep myrtle-beach-golf-and-yacht-club, point the strip on /buyers/affordable-places-to-live/ at it, and 301 /homes/near/golf-and-yacht-club/. (d) In query.js, make a bare town name resolve to the town-* place, or to /homes/?city=, and never to a nohoa-* or second-home-* slice. (e) On each town guide (/submarkets/conway/, /little-river/, /murrells-inlet/, /pawleys-island/, /garden-city/, /surfside-beach/, /north-myrtle-beach/), keep "<town> homes for sale" in the keywords and use the horizontal IDX strip from the town-* place with the heading "Homes for sale in <town> now". The guide is the only indexed answer for that town. (f) Community pages that stay indexed (the-farm, barefoot-resort, prince-creek-55 and others): drop "homes for sale" keywords from the matching guide (for example "The Farm at Carolina Forest homes for sale" on /submarkets/carolina-forest/the-farm/), and let its strip's "See all" link send buyers to the place page.
